subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: latency & peak vs steady-state clarifications
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finex.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput sizing follow-up: latency & peak vs steady-state clarifications

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups to make sure our throughput recommendation matches FinEx's workload. Please confirm the bolded numbers below or correct them inline.

Summary of what we heard (please correct if I misunderstood):
- Use case: synchronous transaction summarization + customer-facing insights endpoint.
- Average prompt length: ~450 tokens (you sent sample batch)
- Average generated response: ~650 tokens
- Steady-state traffic: ~200 QPS
- Peak traffic: bursts to ~1500 QPS for ~2 minutes (daily spikes and marketing events)
- Concurrent sessions (approx): 300–600 active sessions during peak
- Latency SLO: 99th percentile target 300 ms for completed responses (streaming acceptable)
- Streaming: desired for progressive UI; ability to stream partial tokens is important

What we need from you to finalize sizing:
1) Confirm avg prompt/response tokens (or attach updated token profile). I attached the token CSV you shared and annotated it (Attachment: finex_token_profile.csv, CSV, 27KB).
2) Confirm exact steady vs peak QPS numbers and expected burst duration (we heard ~2 min, please confirm).
3) Confirm required p50/p95/p99 latency targets (you mentioned 300ms at p99 but there was a note about faster p95 targets).
4) Any requirements around streaming (max chunk latency, partial output formatting) and client-side concurrency per session.

What Redwood will deliver after you confirm:
- Proposed throughput sizing (GPUs, batch config, expected tokens/sec and QPS per node)
- Suggested model variant(s) and quantization profile to meet p99 latency and cost targets
- Cost ballpark for steady-state vs reserved burst capacity and recommended fallbacks

Next steps: If you can reply with confirmations by EOD Friday, Rafael and I will produce an initial sizing and send a short 30-min follow-up call invite for early next week.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: finex_token_profile.csv (CSV, 27KB)

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finex.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@finex.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: latency & peak vs steady-state clarifications

Neha —

Thanks for the clear summary. Confirming and tightening the numbers after a quick sync with our infra team:
- Average prompt length: 420 tokens (slightly smaller than the sample)
- Average response length: 700 tokens (we pad for safe-side summaries)
- Steady-state traffic: 250 QPS
- Peak traffic: up to 1,800 QPS for ~3 minutes (marketing-triggered spikes)
- Concurrent sessions: target ~500 concurrent active sessions at peak
- Latency targets: aiming for p95 <= 150 ms for short answers; p99 <= 300 ms for full generations
- Streaming: required — we rely on progressive updates for the UI and want partial tokens every ~120ms max

Procurement also asked for a cost estimate for steady-state + peak burst sizing and an outline of any reserved capacity options and associated SLAs.

If you can send a proposed node/config setup + estimated tokens/sec per node and a rough cost delta for reserved burst capacity, we can share this with procurement ahead of the follow-up call.

Appreciate it — Alex
Alex Turner
Senior Product Manager | FinEx
alex.turner@finex.com | +1 (212) 555-0199

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput sizing follow-up: latency & peak vs steady-state clarifications

Adding a technical readout based on Alex's updated numbers (420/700 tokens, steady 250 QPS, peak 1,800 QPS, p99 300ms target, streaming every ~120ms):

Quick sizing back-of-envelope:
- Workload per request: avg tokens ~1120 (prompt + response).
- Tokens/sec requirement:
  - Steady: 250 QPS * 1120 tokens = 280k tokens/sec
  - Peak: 1,800 QPS * 1120 tokens = 2,016k tokens/sec (~2.0M tokens/sec)
- Recommended node type: 8xA100-like GPU pool (dedicated) or equivalent high-throughput inference nodes.
  - Expected sustained tokens/sec per 8x node (with quantized model q4f16 + batching & KV cache): ~200–250k tokens/sec depending on seq length distribution.
  - So steady-state: 2–3 nodes (to hit 280k tokens/sec with buffer).
  - Peak burst: require ~9–11 nodes to hit ~2.0M tokens/sec; recommend autoscaling pool with reserved burst capacity of 8 nodes and fast-spin to 12 for extreme spikes.
- Concurrency / QPS notes: continuous batching helps cost but increases p50; for p99 300ms target we should limit batch window to ~5–8ms and prioritize low-latency queues for interactive traffic.
- Streaming: to guarantee token delivery <=120ms, use streaming-optimized paths (smaller micro-batches, NVLink sharding if available). This increases CPU/network overhead — factor into cost.

Attachments: I put a short note with assumptions and more granular tokens/sec estimates (Attachment: redwood_throughput_notes.pdf).

Open items for sizing accuracy:
- Token distribution tail: need histogram of response lengths (not just mean) — helps refine per-node throughput.
- Peak burst pattern: is it many short spikes (2–3 mins) or sustained multi-hour events? short spikes benefit from reserved burst with warm cache; sustained peaks need more sustained capacity.
- Acceptable fallback model: if we want lower cost for background summarization, provide a fallback lower-capacity model variant — will change node counts.

I'll draft an initial node-level proposal once we get the token histogram and confirmation on burst profile.

— Rafael
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_throughput_notes.pdf (PDF, 68KB)

2) Redwood (Rafael + me): deliver a short proposal by Monday EOD with:

3) Procurement: we'll include a ballpark cost slide for steady + peak and an outline of dedicated vs burst pricing.

I'll send a 30-min follow-up invite for Monday 10am PT. If that doesn't work, reply with slot options.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this sizing so procurement can move forward.
